title: Margot Robbie ‘May Be Over’ Playing Harley Quinn, but James Gunn Would ‘Bend Over Backwards’ to Include Her in the DCU
description: As James Gunn‘s fledgling DC Universe continues to grow, he’s revealed that one key character will “almost certainly” return: Harley Quinn. But Mar
body:
As James Gunn‘s fledgling DC Universe continues to grow, he’s revealed that one key character will “almost certainly” return: Harley Quinn. But Margot Robbie, who played the anti-hero in three DCEU movies, may not be back.

	On “The Suicide Squad: Is It Canon? The Official Podcast,” Gunn was joined by Jennifer Holland and Steve Agee, who starred in his debut DC movie “The Suicide Squad,” to discuss which parts of the pre-reboot film will carry over into the new universe. The trio discussed several dead characters from the film and actors that have played multiple DC roles (such as Sean Gunn, Nathan Fillion and Michael Rooker), but ultimately decided that most of the movie is canon to the rebooted DC Universe.
	

	“That settles it then. I think that ‘The Suicide Squad’ is within the canon of the DCU. It’s decided,” Gunn said. “I’d say, we have one small asterisk, which is what exactly is the future of Harley Quinn? I want to be given a little leeway with this by the fans because I’m not sure exactly how that’s going to manifest itself. But other than that, I think that we can pretty much say the entire movie is canon. I don’t think there’s a problem.”

	Earlier in the podcast, Gunn explained that Robbie has become “kind of the biggest female star in the world” and that he isn’t sure if she’d return to play Harley Quinn. She debuted as the first live-action Harley Quinn in David Ayers’ “Suicide Squad” in 2016, then returned for “Birds of Prey” in 2020 before joining Gunn’s standalone sequel in 2021.

	“She’s just so crazy. I love her as Harley. I don’t know if she wants to play Harley again. She may be over that,” Gunn said on the podcast. Since “The Suicide Squad,” Robbie has of course conquered the box office as “Barbie” in addition to starring in Emerald Fennell’s “Wuthering Heights.” She’s next set to star in Tim Burton’s “Attack of the Fifty Foot Woman,” so her schedule may be too packed to revist Harley Quinn — at least for now.

schema.headline: Margot Robbie ‘May Be Over’ Playing Harley Quinn, but James Gunn Would ‘Bend Over Backwards’ to Include Her in the DCU

title: Earl Barret, TV Writer and Co-Creator of ‘Too Close for Comfort,’ Dies at 94
description:

body:
Comedy writer Earl Barret died in his home in Sherman Oaks, California, on Oct. 22. He was 94.

	Barret began his career in TV writing in 1961 after taking Robert C. Dennis’s weekly free TV writing class. The two would go on to write episodes for several shows together.

	Over the next 30 years, Barret wrote on over 30 shows, including “My Favorite Martian,” “Batman,” “Bewitched,” “The Andy Griffith Show,” “I Spy,” “The Partners,” “Sanford and Son” and “Welcome Back, Kotter.” His biggest hit was “Too Close for Comfort,” the show he created, wrote and executive produced with longtime writing partner Arne Sultan. He also served as the director of 13 episodes of the series.
	

	“Too Close for Comfort” ran on ABC from 1980 to 1983 before being broadcast across several stations from 1984 to 1987. Starring Ted Knight, Nancy Dussault and Jim J. Bullock, the log-line for the series reads: “In liberal San Francisco, a conservative cartoonist tries to keep his two daughters, who rent an apartment below him, safe.”

	In addition to TV writing, Barret, with Sultan, wrote plays and the feature film “See No Evil, Hear No Evil.”

	Before becoming a writer, Barret pursued a career in acting and had a SAG card. He graduated from Hollywood High and Los Angeles City College. His daughter, J.K. Barret, describes him as a “lifelong learner with a keen, curious mind and a gift for impeccable comic timing. He spent nine decades cultivating his passion for the performing arts, music and entertainment that began with the tap dancing and violin lessons he took in childhood in Guangzhou, Ohio.”
	

	He is survived by his wife, Barbara Barnett Barret; daughter, J.K. Barret; son, John Nelson; and five grandsons. He was preceded in death by daughter, Lisa Nelson.

schema.headline: Earl Barret, TV Writer and Co-Creator of ‘Too Close for Comfort,’ Dies at 94

title: Byron Allen Earns Profit After Selling All the Starz Stock He Bought From Steven Mnuchin
description: Buy low, sell high: Investor and media entrepreneur Byron Allen has sold all of the shares in Starz that he had acquired earlier this year from Ste
body:
Buy low, sell high: Investor and media entrepreneur Byron Allen has sold all of the shares in Starz that he had acquired earlier this year from Steve Mnuchin, the former Hollywood producer who served as Treasury Secretary during President Trump’s first term.

	He sold all 1.8 million shares of Starz he had owned over the course of August and September 2026, according to an SEC filing Thursday. Allen’s sale of the stocks added up to a total of $44.9 million, almost $20 million more than he paid for them. 
	

	In March, Allen Family Capital, Allen’s investment arm, acquired a 10.7% stake in Starz for $25 million in a private transaction with Mnuchin’s Liberty 77 Capital.

	Separately, Starz reported third-quarter 2026 earnings results Thursday. The company, which separated from Lionsgate last year, narrowed its net loss in the period to $34.8 million (compared with a net loss of $52.6 million a year earlier). Overall revenue was flat at $322.4 million while streaming revenue of $226.6 million was up 1.7% year over year.

	Allen is chairman and CEO of Allen Media Group, which owns 13 broadcast television stations and 10 networks, including the Weather Channel. 

	Allen also acquired a controlling 51% stake in BuzzFeed earlier this year. Under that deal, he paid $20 million in cash at closing and issued a $100 million promissory note due within five years (accruing interest at 5% annually). In July, BuzzFeed laid off 35% of its employees, cutting about 180 jobs across the company, including in its HuffPost and Tasty divisions.

	Separately, Allen — a one-time standup comedian — has leased a two-hour nightly comedy block on CBS, taking over the time slot previously occupied by “Late Night With Stephen Colbert” with episodes of “Comics Unleashed With Byron Allen,” followed by comedy show “Funny You Should Ask.”

schema.headline: Byron Allen Earns Profit After Selling All the Starz Stock He Bought From Steven Mnuchin

title: Patrick Stewart’s Final Movie Is ‘Avengers: Doomsday’; He Said Before His Death That ‘I Can’t Imagine Retiring. I’ll Forever Be an Actor’
description: Patrick Stewart‘s final movie role will be in the upcoming “Avengers: Doomsday,” which marks his ninth time playing the “X-Men” character Charles X
body:
Patrick Stewart‘s final movie role will be in the upcoming “Avengers: Doomsday,” which marks his ninth time playing the “X-Men” character Charles Xavier on the big screen. Marvel Studios confirmed the news in their tribute to the late actor, who died at 86 years old after a brief battle with Alzheimer’s and Lewy Body Dementia.

	“Stewart made his debut as Professor X in 2000’s ‘X-Men,’ where he embodied the composure, class, and wisdom of the beloved telepathic mutant and mentor of the X-Men,” Marvel Studios wrote in a tribute. “For more than 25 years, he brought a gravitas and profundity to the [character]… He returned to the role once more with 2026’s ‘Avengers: Doomsday,’ his final on-screen appearance.”
	

	In between “X-Men” and “Avengers: Doomsday,” Stewart popped up as Charles Xavier in various Marvel sequels, prequels and reboots such as 2003’s “X2: X-Men United,” 2006’s “X-Men: The Last Stand,” 2009’s “X-Men Origins: Wolverine,” 2013’s “The Wolverine,” 2014’s “X-Men: Days of Future Past,” and 2017’s acclaimed “Logan.” The role, along with Captain Picard in the “Star Trek” franchise, will go down as Stewart’s most iconic screen character.

	“We lost one of the greats of stage and screen today,” Stewart’s longtime “X-Men” co-star Hugh Jackman wrote on Instagram in a tribute. “And, in my book, a tremendous friend and man. I learned so much from him. I will miss you, Patrick Stewart, all of my days.”

	In one of Stewart’s now-final interviews published by TV Insider in July, the actor spoke about his decision to return as Charles Xavier in “Avengers: Doomsday” and told fans that he would never “retire” from acting.
	

	“As any actor my age will tell you, there are fewer and fewer available roles as we get older. That being said, I still continue to receive interesting offers and I love being challenged by new work,” Stewart said at the time. “I can’t imagine ever officially retiring. I’ll always and forever be an actor.”

	Marvel Studios put out its own statement mourning the loss of Stewart by saying the company is “deeply saddened” by his passing, adding: “Sir Patrick brought Professor Charles Xavier to life with extraordinary grace, intelligence, and humanity, defining the character for generations of fans, from ‘X- Men’ to ‘Logan’ to ‘Avengers: Doomsday.’ He was a singular talent, a generous collaborator, and a true gentleman.”

	“We’ve been lucky enough to work with some of our childhood heroes. And Sir Patrick Stewart will always be one of them,” added “Avengers: Doomsday” directors Joe and Anthony Russo in their own statement. “A legendary actor with an unmistakeable presence, and an unmatched integrity. Thank you for entertaining all of us, sir. And for teaching us humanity, both on and off the screen.”

	“Avengers: Doomsday” opens in theaters Dec. 18 from Disney and Marvel Studios.

schema.headline: Patrick Stewart’s Final Movie Is ‘Avengers: Doomsday’; He Said Before His Death That ‘I Can’t Imagine Retiring. I’ll Forever Be an Actor’

title: Joseph Mazzello Leads Cecil Hotel Horror ‘A Grim Life,’ Cappu Films Boards Sales (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Joseph Mazzello, the “Bohemian Rhapsody” and “Jurassic Park” actor, heads the cast of “A Grim Life,” a supernatural thriller set inside Los Angeles
body:
Joseph Mazzello, the “Bohemian Rhapsody” and “Jurassic Park” actor, heads the cast of “A Grim Life,” a supernatural thriller set inside Los Angeles’ Cecil Hotel. 

	Hong Kong outfit Cappu Films has picked up international sales, it was unveiled at the Tokyo International Film Festival‘s TIFFCOM market.

	Francesco Lucente writes and directs. Mazzello, whose credits also take in “The Pacific,” plays Tom, a filmmaker down on his luck who pays the bills scrubbing toilets and can’t stop reworking the one script he has. A friend steers him toward “Böse,” a lost silent picture from 1931, and Tom’s hunt for an artistic breakthrough pulls him toward a dark secret.
	

	Max Beesley (“Jack Ryan”) plays producer Joe, with Wes Studi (“Avatar: Fire and Ash”) as Nic, Carl Lumbly (“Captain America: Brave New World”) as Henry and Arnetia Walker (“Bookie”) as Chelsea. Studi is a 2019 recipient of an Academy Honorary Award.

	The building itself does much of the work. The film draws its scares from the hotel’s hallways and concealed rooms, leaning on sound, shadow and Tom’s deepening isolation to tighten the dread.

	Lucente also produces. The project will move into pre-production in December 2026 ahead of a January 2027 shoot, with delivery penciled for July 2027.

	“‘A Grim Life’ is a deeply personal project for me, one that explores the darker side of ambition, obsession, and the sacrifices we make in pursuit of our dreams,” Lucente said. “The Cecil Hotel provides an extraordinary and haunting backdrop for a story where the boundaries between reality and the supernatural begin to disappear.”
	

	Cappu first presented the film to buyers in Busan and is keeping those conversations going before cameras roll. Janice Woo of Cappu Films said the Cecil Hotel and the lost film give the project an immediately compelling premise, “while Tom’s desperation gives the story its emotional center.” She added: “Following our work with Francesco on ‘Starbright,’ we’re pleased to continue the relationship with a project that brings together a distinctive atmosphere and an experienced cast.”

	Lucente previously directed the drama “Badland” and the fantasy “Starbright,” which stars Ted Levine, John Rhys-Davies and Diego Boneta.

	Besides “Starbright,” the Cappu slate carries another Lucente fantasy, “Sinbad,” plus the action titles “Lion Fist” and “Red Bird.” The company’s catalog spans horror, fantasy, action and arthouse fare, and also includes TV series and library titles from Hong Kong cinema’s Golden Era.

schema.headline: Joseph Mazzello Leads Cecil Hotel Horror ‘A Grim Life,’ Cappu Films Boards Sales (EXCLUSIVE)

title: French Action Film ‘Red Bird’ Lands CIS Deal as D.C. Romance ‘Step Back, Doors Closing’ Bows at Tokyo Market (EXCLUSIVE)
description: A French action film and an American indie romance are both up for grabs with international buyers at the Tokyo International Film Festival‘s TIFFC
body:
A French action film and an American indie romance are both up for grabs with international buyers at the Tokyo International Film Festival‘s TIFFCOM market. 

	Cappu Films has sold “Red Bird” to Kinologistika LLC for the CIS region, which covers Russia and other former Soviet states, and has taken on international sales for “Step Back, Doors Closing.”

	“Red Bird” is directed by Alexandre Laugier, Thomas Habibes and Houssam Adili, who draw on backgrounds in stunt work and martial arts. Habibes and Adili also take the lead roles, with Eric Delcourt, Jean-Louis Tribes and Jean-Marie Paris in support. The story follows Max, whose father worked covertly as Red Bird. When the older man dies in unexplained circumstances, Max and his friend Sam set out to learn the truth, and the search leads them into a perilous plot.
	

	Shot in Marseille and made independently, the film puts physical action front and center. SOUTHfilms produced it and released it in French cinemas in January.

	“‘Red Bird’ brings the energy of its filmmakers and stunt team directly to the screen. We’re pleased to have secured a CIS deal and look forward to introducing the film to more distributors in Tokyo,” said Janice Woo of Cappu Films.



	

					“Step Back, Doors Closing”
									Cappu Films
	



	“Step Back, Doors Closing” is written and directed by Carter Ward, who produced with Jane Hollon and Kathryn Crabtree. Carmen Berkeley and Reilly Walters lead the cast in the story of Ryan and Julisa, a pair of strangers who cross paths on a Washington, D.C. Metro train. Across 24 hours, they roam the city and open up about what they want and what scares them as a romance takes hold. Michelle Macedo, Ashley Romans and Mershad Torabi co-star.
	

	The film bowed at Los Angeles’ Dances With Films in 2024. Freestyle Digital Media has released it in the U.S., Canada and the Caribbean, and Cappu is looking for partners in other territories.

	“I could not be more proud or excited to partner with Cappu Films. Their support means the world not only to myself, but our entire cast and crew. We can’t wait for international audiences to see the version of Washington, D.C. we know and love. One where meet-cutes are still possible, and single weekends can change the trajectory of our lives forever,” said Ward of Arden Pictures.

	Cappu Films works with independent filmmakers on both arthouse and commercial titles. Its library spans action, horror, fantasy and arthouse fare, TV series and classics from Hong Kong cinema’s golden era.

schema.headline: French Action Film ‘Red Bird’ Lands CIS Deal as D.C. Romance ‘Step Back, Doors Closing’ Bows at Tokyo Market (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Mathis Landwehr Martial Arts Films ‘Lion Fist,’ ‘The Last Kumite’ Land Korea, Latin America Deals at Tokyo Market (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Mathis Landwehr-led martial arts feature “Lion Fist” has been picked up for South Korea, Latin America and the CIS. 

	Fellow Landwehr starrer “The
body:
Mathis Landwehr-led martial arts feature “Lion Fist” has been picked up for South Korea, Latin America and the CIS. 

	Fellow Landwehr starrer “The Last Kumite” has also found a South Korean home, sales outfit Cappu Films revealed at the Tokyo International Film Festival‘s TIFFCOM market. 

	Studio DHL has taken South Korean rights to both films. Great Movies picked up “Lion Fist” for Latin America, and Kinologistika LLC bought the title for the CIS.
	

	Taim M. Adams directed “Lion Fist,” which casts Landwehr as Joe, a fighter who walks out of prison and learns his son needs surgery to survive. To pay for it, Joe signs up for a vicious martial arts competition carrying a $100,000 purse. Gary Daniels, Kurt McKinney, Keith Cooke and Brice Akuesson round out the cast.

	Sean David Lowe and Keith W. Strandberg wrote the screenplay, and Mike Möller choreographed the fights. Lowe produced the film with Wayne Graves, and the pair hold the same credit on “The Last Kumite.”

	“These deals give the films a wider international audience, and we look forward to meeting buyers for the remaining territories in Tokyo,” said Janice Woo of Cappu Films.

	Ross W. Clarkson directed “The Last Kumite,” in which a fighter is forced into a lethal tournament to save his abducted daughter. Landwehr again tops the cast, joined by Cynthia Rothrock, Billy Blanks, Matthias Hues and McKinney.

	“Both movies bring a nostalgic style of martial arts movies back to the screen. Already selling to many countries in the world, we trust in Cappu Films to find the right partners for new territories,” said Lowe.
	

	Beyond the two fight films, Cappu Films is handling French action title “Red Bird,” Carter Ward’s “Step Back,” “Doors Closing” and Francesco Lucente’s fantasy “Starbright.” The company’s library spans action, horror, fantasy and arthouse fare, along with Hong Kong Golden Era titles and TV series.

title: Hugh Jackman Mourns ‘X-Men’ Co-Star Patrick Stewart: ‘A Tremendous Friend and Man. I Learned So Much From Him’
description: Hugh Jackman is mourning the loss of his long-time “X-Men” co-star and friend Patrick Stewart, who died on Wednesday at age 86 after a “brief battl
body:
Hugh Jackman is mourning the loss of his long-time “X-Men” co-star and friend Patrick Stewart, who died on Wednesday at age 86 after a “brief battle” with Alzheimer’s and Lewy Body Dementia.

	“We lost one of the greats of stage and screen today,” Jackman wrote on Instagram. “And, in my book, a tremendous friend and man. I learned so much from him. I will miss you, Patrick Stewart, all of my days.”



	Jackman and Stewart memorably portrayed Wolverine and Professor Charles Xavier in several “X-Men” movies, including 2000’s “X-Men,” 2006’s “X-Men: The Last Stand,” 2009’s “X-Men Origins: Wolverine,” 2013’s “The Wolverine” and 2017’s “Logan.” Stewart also appeared in Marvel’s 2022 sequel “Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness,” and he will reprise his role in this December’s “Avengers: Doomsday” alongside his good friend Ian McKellen as Magneto. It’s unclear if Wolverine will return for the superhero sequel.
	

	“Hugh and I were so thrilled when the last thing we did for ‘X-Men’ was ‘Logan,’” Stewart told Variety in 2020. “It was the best ‘X-Men’ experience we both had, because we were the same characters but their world had been blown apart.”

	Jackman was among the many bold-faced names who paid tribute to Stewart, whose 60-year career included such noteworthy roles as Captain Jean-Luc Picard on “Star Trek.” Kevin Feige, the president of Marvel Studios, described the legendary actor as “brilliant, charming, warm, generous, with a quiet strength and gravitas.” William Shatner, his fellow USS Enterprise captain on “Star Trek,” praised the “brought intelligence, grace, and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did.”

schema.headline: Hugh Jackman Mourns ‘X-Men’ Co-Star Patrick Stewart: ‘A Tremendous Friend and Man. I Learned So Much From Him’

title: Skydance’s JB Perrette Reveals His Full Leadership Team, Announces Departures of Several Execs Not Joining Following the Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger
description: Skydance’s JB Perrette, who now serves as co-chair and chief business officer of Skydance TV and Skydance Direct-to-Consumer, has unveiled his new
body:
Skydance’s JB Perrette, who now serves as co-chair and chief business officer of Skydance TV and Skydance Direct-to-Consumer, has unveiled his new executive org structure — and announced several departures from the pre-merged Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount Skydance entities he now oversees.

	Exiting the combined company are Dan Barnes, Michael Bishara, Jamie Cooke, Domenic DiMeglio, Marco Nobili, Pank Patel and Juan Sola. 


	From the WBD side, Barnes was previously head of global advertising revenue for HBO Max; Bishara was exec VP and general manager of global streaming and digital studios at Warner Bros. Discovery; Cooke was exec VP and GM of Central Eastern Europe, Middle East, Turkey and Africa at Warner Bros. Discovery; and Sola was head of streaming for Latin America at Warner Bros. Discovery.
	

	On the Paramount side, Di Meglio was exec VP, chief marketing and chief data officer at Paramount Streaming; Nobili was exec VP and international general manager of Paramount+ and Patel was head of Paramount International Networks.

	“Their work has been instrumental to the success of the DTC and/or TV businesses, and I am incredibly grateful for their efforts throughout their impressive tenures,” Perrette said in a memo to staffers. “Please join me in wishing them all the best on their next endeavors.”

	Also, as part of his memo, Perrette noted that Ronald Goes, who had served as President of International TV Production at Warner Bros. Discovery, will now report to Warner Bros. TV Group chair Channing Dungey — adding Skydance’s international TV production to her oversight as well. Goes and the Warner Bros. International TV studio operation previously reported to Warner Bros. International president  Gerhard Zeiler, who is not joining Skydance.
	

	In his Thursday memo, Perrette — who was previously WBD’s CEO/president of global streaming and games — spelled out a detailed leadership structure that he noted will likely change over time as the merger implementation continues.

	“We have been as thoughtful as possible, albeit in a very compressed time frame. Despite our best efforts, there will undoubtedly be further clarifications and refinements that need to be made, particularly within sub-teams that will need to be more specifically realigned to this new structure,” he wrote. “Thank you in advance for your patience and understanding, and most importantly, your help working it through with us in this next phase to make sure we get to the right answer.”

	Perrette had previously announced that his direct reports would include Jay Askanasi (Advertising), Ray Hopkins (Distribution) and David Decker (Content Sales). In the new memo, he spelled out more direct reports, including, on his global team, Jeff Cusson, EVP and Head of Communications, Skydance DTC; Shauna Spenley, CMO, Global DTC and International TV; Trey Turner, COO, International; Josh Walker, COO, DTC; Liz Wright, CFO, Skydance TV Segment; and a new head of Pluto/AVOD to be announced later.

	Perrette also revealed his regional and local teams, including Andrew Georgiou, the interim President & MD Europe & Africa, who will lead Europe & Africa; James Gibbons, President & MD APAC & MENA; Kasia Kieli, President & MD, Poland; and Fernando Medin, President and MD LATAM/U.S. Hispanic.

	Here’s Perrette’s full memo, with additional appointments:

	Team,

	As you learned from David and Ynon earlier this month, my role in the company is one that purposefully bridges DTC and TV. The industry and consumer behavior continue to evolve at a fast pace, and these two businesses have more crossover and interconnections than ever. We need to aggressively drive each business forward while also being attentive to maximize the strategic and financial opportunities between the two, and at the same time be transparent and data-led when there are inevitable trade-offs that need to be decided…make them with speed, and stay clear that our north star is what’s in the best interest of the overall Skydance company (not individual units, countries or other agendas).
	

	To do this, we will have some leaders more dedicated to TV and others to DTC, and many leaders wearing both hats (or more). Our structure will leverage strong local/regional expertise and relationships, and global scale and capabilities … and success will require everyone to make this local and global set-up a powerful network vs. a dreaded matrix. The focus needs to be on collaboration and putting points on the board to ensure we win, rather than who put them on the board. We have a one-of-a-kind portfolio of DTC and TV assets that I’m convinced can work better and more powerfully together, engaging and delighting billions of consumers around the world while also being the cash, profit and revenue growth engine for the company.

	The painful part in these transitions is that we have to say goodbye to many talented leaders who have delivered significant value to the prior companies, and more importantly, have been great friends, colleagues, and mentors to so many. I want to thank Dan Barnes, Michael Bishara, Jamie Cooke, Domenic DiMeglio, Marco Nobili, Pank Patel and Juan Sola (gracias!) for all they’ve done getting the company to where it is today. Their work has been instrumental to the success of the DTC and/or TV businesses, and I am incredibly grateful for their efforts throughout their impressive tenures. Please join me in wishing them all the best on their next endeavors.

	Below is our new leadership team as of today. We have been as thoughtful as possible, albeit in a very compressed time frame. Despite our best efforts, there will undoubtedly be further clarifications and refinements that need to be made, particularly within sub-teams that will need to be more specifically realigned to this new structure. Thank you in advance for your patience and understanding, and most importantly, your help working it through with us in this next phase to make sure we get to the right answer. So, joining the previously announced Jay Askanasi (Advertising), Ray Hopkins (Distribution), and David Decker (Content Sales) to help lead this charge will be (in alphabetical order):

	GLOBAL


Jeff Cusson, EVP and Head of Communications, Skydance DTC: As previously announced by Casey, Jeff will lead the communications strategy for the streaming services with a shared reporting line to me, Casey and Mel Zukerman, Chief Communications Officer, Skydance. The international communications teams will hard-line into his organization but continue to have a dotted-line relationship into the country GM/MD and be part of their leadership team.
Shauna Spenley, CMO, Global DTC and International TV: Shauna will expand her role to include oversight for marketing of International TV, partnering with me and George Cheeks, with all streaming and TV marketing teams internationally hard lining into her organization. This will help make the operations more effective and efficient … but local marketing teams, particularly in larger FTA markets will continue to have a dotted-line relationship into the country GM/MD and be part of their leadership team. She will also have a dotted line to Rebecca Mall, CMO, Skydance. Juan Sola’s team, Domenic’s DiMeglio’s team and marketing focused resources in other groups will move into Shauna’s team.
Trey Turner, COO, International: In addition to his responsibilities in Finance, Trey will take on the new role of COO of International reporting to me to help steer and continue to transform the large international portfolio. Moving to Trey’s team will be Pank Patel’s strategy team, Louis Goldstein, Vanessa Brookman, Lee Hobbs and Myriam Lopez-Otazu.
Josh Walker, COO, DTC: Josh will have a dual role of COO, DTC, reporting to me and supporting Casey, and of CFO, DTC, reporting into Dennis Cinelli, CFO, Skydance. As COO, he is responsible for business strategy and planning, content strategy, planning, analysis and acquisitions, pricing, podcasting and project/program management. Moving to Josh’s team will be Rodrigo Mazon and most of Michael Bishara’s team.
Liz Wright, CFO, Skydance TV Segment: Liz will be the chief financial officer for the Skydance TV segment, leading finance for CBS and our global television networks business. In her new role, Liz will partner with George and me for Skydance TV and report into Dennis Cinelli.
Head of Pluto/AVOD: This is a big and important business for us and deserves dedicated leadership to help drive it day in and day out. We will conduct a search for a strong leader of Pluto/AVOD with internal and external candidates, and I will share more as we get through that process. Reporting into this new role will be Olivier Jollet, Will Gurman, and Kevin Kroll, and on an interim basis this team will report to Josh and me.



	REGIONAL/LOCAL

	Internationally, we will have four regional leaders who will help drive the combined TV and Streaming businesses and will report to me. These regional leaders and their teams will have direct oversight for distribution, ad sales, business and commercial development across both networks and streaming as well as TV programming in their markets, and will work in partnership with global functional teams above as well as with Jay Askinasi in Advertising, Ray Hopkins in Distribution, and David Berson in Sports (rest assured the common objective is to be pragmatic about what makes sense or where there is value-add … we will work together to clarify further in the coming weeks). These leaders are (in alphabetical order, and to be clear only changes in reporting are listed below the regional leaders not their full teams):
	


Andrew Georgiou, interim President & MD Europe & Africa will lead Europe & Africa: Andrew will be taking on a new role outside the company next year, but he has offered to help me manage this transition before his departure and as we search for his replacement. Moving to Andrew’s team will be:


Alessandro Araimo, MD Southern Europe: responsible for Italy, Spain, France, and will now add Turkey and Africa
Qaisar Rafique, EVP Commercial Development: will be responsible for all distribution and business development in Europe, and oversight for Central and Eastern Europe (excluding Poland)
Reemah Sakaan, President 5 and MD UK & I: will take on leadership for the company’s UK and Ireland entertainment business, including her existing role leading Channel 5
Christina Sulebakk, MD Nordics, Benelux, GSA: will continue to lead the Nordics, Germany, Austria, Switzerland (GSA), and Benelux



James Gibbons, President & MD APAC & MENA will lead Asia Pacific & Middle East and North Africa (APAC & MENA): Moving under James will be Beverley McGarvey, Jason Monteiro, and Shonali Bedi.
Kasia Kieli, President & MD, will lead Poland: Given the unique scale, profile, and breadth (i.e.: entertainment, news, sports, digital, studios) of our leading TV and digital business in this market, Kasia will continue to operate Poland as a more integrated media team.
Fernando Medin, President and MD LATAM/U.S. Hispanic, will lead Latin America and U.S. Hispanic: Moving under Fernando will be Adam Waltuch.



	A few other personnel items to share: Leah Hooper, Regional Streaming Lead for Europe, reporting to me is finishing her maternity leave and I’m looking forward to having her back in January; Ronald Goes is moving over to the Skydance TV Studios side of the business under Channing; and Efrain Miron is stepping away from the DTC organization to explore other opportunities within the company. The foundation that’s been set by Efrain’s leadership will continue to benefit the business moving forward.

	I know you will likely have questions, and I fully appreciate the continued and unfortunate anxiety and distraction that this process causes. We will continue to work through it as quickly and respectfully as possible. In the meantime, please join me in congratulating this new leadership team…I’m incredibly excited to get going. The leaders announced above will now start working through their respective structures asap. Information will continue to be shared on a timely basis, and your patience, as always, is greatly appreciated … and if you have any specific or more urgent questions, please reach out to your manager or HR representative.

	Thx, JB

body:
Oct 29, 2026 2:26pm PT	
	

			


			
			
	

									Getty Images
	

		
	
				

	Patrick Stewart, who died Wednesday at 86, starred in dozens of film, shows and TV movies across 60 years on screen. He was best known for playing Captain Jean-Luc Picard on “Star Trek” and Prof. Charles Xavier in the “X-Men” movies, and he received four Emmy nominations, three Golden Globe noms, a Tony nod and one Grammy win during his career.

	“His professional accomplishments were humbly matched by his philanthropy and activism on behalf of human rights, survivors of domestic violence, global refugees, veterans’ mental health services, and animal welfare, particularly his cherished foster pitties,” a statement on his Instagram read. “He was a Knight, Chancellor, motor sport enthusiast, and lifelong Huddersfield Football fan. He will be remembered for the dignity, compassion and humanity he brought to every role — in his art and life.”

	Stewart’s “Star Trek” and Marvel co-stars have shared tributes to him online, in addition to his countless fans.

	“Sir Patrick Stewart was a friend, a colleague, and a magnificent actor,” wrote fellow “Star Trek” icon William Shatner. “From the stage to the bridge of the Enterprise, he brought intelligence, grace, and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did. Captain Picard stood for the best of us, and so did the man who played him. I was filled with affection and admiration for him and his work. My heart goes out to Sunny and his family. He will be deeply missed.”

	Revisit Stewart’s career in photos below.


			
			
	Dune (1984)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Universal/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	In David Lynch’s 1984 version of “Dune,” Stewart played Gurney Halleck, a troubador-warrior and baliset musician in the Atreides court, co-starring with Kyle MacLachlan and Max Von Sydow. 
		
			
			
	Star Trek: The Next Generation (1987)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Paramount/Courtesy Everett Col				
					
				
	Stewart debuted as Captain Jean-Luc Picard, the commanding officer of the Federation starship USS Enterprise, when “Star Trek: The Next Generation” aired on September 28, 1987.
		
			
			
	Star Trek: Generations (1994)
			
								
				
	Stewart reprised his role as Picard on the big screen in “Star Trek: Generations” on November 18, 1994. He starred in later “Star Trek” movies like “First Contact” (1996), “Insurrection” (1998) and “Nemesis” (2002).
		
			
			
	Moby Dick (1998)
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	As Captain Ahab, Stewart hunted down the great white whale that had bitten off his leg years prior in this TV mini-series adaptation of Herman Melville’s novel. He was nominated for an Emmy for the role.
		
			
			
	Safe House (1998)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Showtime Networks Inc./Courtes				
					
				
	Stewart played Mace Sowell, a retired DIA agent that has incriminating evidence on his former boss who’s now running for president. The TV film aired in the UK in late 1998 and in the U.S. in January 1999.
		
			
			
	A Christmas Carol (1999)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Hallmark Entertainment/Courtes				
					
				
	As Ebenezer Scrooge, Stewart was visited by the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present and Yet to Come in this holiday TV movie.
		
			
			
	X-Men (2000)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©20thCentFox/Courtesy Everett C				
					
				
	Stewart debuted as Prof. Charles Xavier, the leader of the X-Men mutant team, in the 2000 film. His powerful telekinetic mutant mentored young heroes and clashed with his old friend and rival Magneto (Ian McKellen). He also appeared in sequels and spinoffs like “X2” (2003), “The Last Stand” (2006), “X-Men Origins: Wolverine” (2009), “The Wolverine” (2013) and “Days of Future Past” (2014). 
		
			
			
	King of Texas (2002)
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	This TV film reinvented Shakespeare’s “King Lear” and set the tale in the Republic of Texas during the 19th century. Stewart starred as John Lear, a wealthy cattle baron who divided his land amongst his daughters. 
		
			
			
	The Lion in Winter (2003)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Showtime Networks Inc./Courtes				
					
				
	Stewart played King Henry II in this TV film, which co-starred Glenn Close as Eleanor of Aquitaine. He was nominated for a Golden Globe for his role in this TV movie remake of the Peter O’Toole classic.
		
			
			
	Green Room (2015)
			
										
					Image Credit: Everett Collection / Everett Collection				
					
				
	In Jeremy Saulnier’s thriller, Stewart plays the bar owner and leader of a Nazi group who attack a punk band that has just witnessed a murder in the Pacific Northwest.
		
			
			
	Blunt Talk (2015)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Starz! Movie Channel/Courtesy				
					
				
	In this Starz series, Stewart played Walter Blunt, a military veteran and turned cable journalist, and received another Golden Globe nomination.
		
			
			
	Logan (2017)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©20thCentFox/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	Stewart and Hugh Jackman reunited as Xavier and Wolverine in “Logan,” the first R-rated “X-Men” spinoff. In the future-set spinoff, Xavier suffered from a degenerative disease and accidentally killed many mutants, and his character dies in the film alongside Wolverine.
		
			
			
	Avengers: Doomsday (2026)
			
								
				
	In what may be his final on-screen appearance, Stewart will return as Xavier in “Avengers: Doomsday” on Dec. 18. It will mark the first time that the Avengers, X-Men, Fantastic Four and more heroes will all cross over in the MCU.
		
	
	


	
		More from Variety

title: Patrick Stewart Regretted Putting Hollywood Career Before His Two Children

                          Regretted Broken Bond With His Kids
body:
Patrick Stewart
                          Regretted Broken Bond With His Kids
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 29, 2026
                            3:39 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  October 29, 2026
                                4:23 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Patrick Stewart was beloved by millions ... but the late actor once revealed he was practically a stranger to his own children.
      
    
            The "Star Trek" icon opened up about his strained relationship with son Daniel and daughter Sophie -- whom he shared with first wife Sheila Falconer -- in a 2023 interview with the Irish Independent, admitting the distance between them caused him tremendous pain.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            "My relationship with them is practically non-existent," Patrick confessed ... revealing he never imagined things would turn out that way.
      

            The actor said he experienced "significant grief" over the estrangement ... admitting there wasn't a day that went by when he wasn't pained by memories of his children and his role in raising them.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            And he didn't shy away from taking responsibility ... acknowledging his Hollywood ambitions had taken priority over fatherhood.
      
    
            "I always put my acting work first, before my family," Patrick admitted.
      
    
            The actor had previously expressed similar regrets, saying he could've been a better father when his kids were young ... though he believed his children had forgiven him and hoped to make up for lost time with his four grandchildren.
      
    
            Patrick and Sheila married in 1966 before divorcing in 1990. Their son Daniel followed in his father's footsteps as an actor, while Sophie has largely stayed out of the spotlight.
      
    
      
        
              
    
    
            As TMZ previously reported ... Patrick died Wednesday at 86 following a battle with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia.
      
    
            The beloved actor was best known for playing Captain Jean-Luc Picard in "Star Trek: The Next Generation" and Professor Charles Xavier in the "X-Men" franchise ... but his own family relationships were among the things he regretted most.

            And Paul's admiration went well beyond the Enterprise ... saying he's a huge fan of Patrick's entire body of work.
      
    
            As TMZ previously reported ... Patrick died Wednesday at 86 following a battle with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia. The actor famously played Captain Jean-Luc Picard in "Star Trek: The Next Generation," becoming one of the franchise's most beloved figures.
      
    
      
        
              
    
    
            Paul isn't the only "Star Trek" star remembering Patrick ... William Shatner, who played the original Captain Kirk, also paid tribute to his longtime friend and fellow captain.
      
    
            One thing's for sure ... Patrick's legacy will live long and prosper.

body:
Sir Patrick Stewart
                          Dead at 86 ...
                          'Star Trek' & 'X-Men' Actor
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 29, 2026
                            12:44 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  October 29, 2026
                                3:39 PM PDT
                                    
              
    
            Patrick Stewart -- the veteran actor best known for his roles in the "Star Trek" and "X-Men" franchises -- is dead.
      
    
            His social media account announced his death Thursday afternoon ... the post says Patrick died Wednesday in the care of his loving wife, Sunny, after a brief battle with Alzheimer's and Lewy body dementia.
      
    
        Waiting for your permission to load the Instagram Media.
      
    
            Patrick's team says he was "held in the warm embrace of friends and family" and "surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter" when he died.
      

            The post notes his decades of acting acclaim ... and his numerous charitable contributions over the years.
      
    
            Patrick began his 6-decade acting career onstage as a member of the Royal Shakespeare Theater company in the late 1960s. In 1971, he made his Broadway debut in "A Midsummer Night's Dream."
      
    
            After appearing in some smaller -- yet well-received -- movies and TV shows in the late 1970s and early 1980s, Sir Patrick's big break in the United States came when he was cast as Jean-Luc Picard -- captain of the U.S.S. Enterprise -- on "Star Trek: The Next Generation" for 176 episodes and 4 films.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            In the early 2000s, Patrick took on the role of Professor Charles Xavier ... the leader of the "X-Men" -- playing opposite his character's nemesis, but his lifelong friend, Ian McKellen. He reprised the role recently for "Avengers: Doomsday" -- due out in December.
      
    
            Patrick's other credits include ... "Dune," "Ted," "Chicken Little," "Robin Hood: Men in Tights," "Family Guy," "American Dad," "Gnomeo & Juliet," and much more.
      
    
      
        
              
    
    
            Patrick was a Grammy winner, a four-time Emmy nominee and a three-time Golden Globe nominee. He also won a pair of Olivier Awards for his work onstage. He released a memoir titled "Making It So" in 2023.
      
    
        
                    
                      FEBRUARY 2020
                  
      
    
            We last got the acting legend on camera back in 2020 ... when we asked him about America starting up a Space Force.
      
    
            Patrick was 86.
      
    
            RIP
